business_rules.statement: The platform computes the identity's audit read scope from role and scope, never from a stored preference, and the query is bounded to permitted event classes before execution so unauthorised classes are never retrieved and then filtered.
All nine role types are written into the audit log for every action they take.
business_rules.applies_to: All nine human security role types

business_rules.statement: An empty result and a forbidden result must not look alike; a reader never sees a filter for a class they cannot read.

Command Center actions are commands executed through Hub services, the same services the Hub's own screens use, with identical rules, producing a Hub-owned audit event rather than a separate Command Center log.
No audit reader exists on the Command Center or the Frontline.

The audit log is append-only and immutable, with no delete or edit path on any surface. A correction is never a modification and never a deletion: it is a new audit event of a correction class carrying a correction-target reference, corrected values within the allowlist, correcting identity, correction time and a mandatory reason.
No surface offers a delete or edit control on any committed record or audit event; the surface offers Correct, never Edit.

The platform never presents stale data as current: where a recompute fails the record is marked 'Corrected; figures not yet recomputed' and stale figures are shown side by side with the staleness stated.

Commit-together rule at device scope: a business event and its audit event either both enter the local durable append-only queue or neither does; on sync the server commits both in one server transaction.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Device local transaction and server transaction

business_rules.statement: A device that cannot write its audit queue blocks capture and preserves existing work; the device enters an upload-only state.
Quarantine never splits a business event from its audit event.
The device retains no audit content after server confirmation, because the tenant log is the record of truth.
No severity classification event carries an agent contribution field; detection is deterministic and no artificial-intelligence model sits in the deviation-triggering path.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Audit event schema and build-time test

business_rules.statement: An agent may never elevate its permissions, change tenant scope, impersonate a role, self-approve, release a Severity 1 hold, bypass a gate, classify deviations, execute stale queued actions, or delete evidence or audit history; every attempt is refused and recorded under EVT-RES-AI.
Agent output that cannot be accompanied by a decision record is not delivered, because an agent contribution that cannot be explained afterwards must not influence a decision now.
A notification that cannot be audited is not sent.
Exactly three access classes exist and no path reaches tenant content outside them; no ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
A compliance-emergency session requires two distinct authorising identities: the root plus one Admin. Neither alone opens the session.
Mirroring into the tenant's log occurs continuously during a session, not at close.
A privileged session that cannot be audited terminates automatically.
Scope is applied before assembly; out-of-scope events never appear, including as counts.
A partial result is never presented as complete; a partial export is never delivered without an explicit partial label.
No V1 claim of cryptographic tamper-evidence appears on any surface or in any export.
No code path deletes an audit record except a compliance-driven deletion naming its standard.
Anonymisation severs identity resolution and never rewrites audit rows; the audit event continues to carry the same worker identifier and that identifier ceases to resolve to a person.
Regulated-Industry mode tenants never anonymise, and switching a tenant into Regulated-Industry mode later does not resurrect anonymised identities.
The audit log's lifetime is never shorter than the data it evidences.
No privileged, destructive, approval, publication, release, security, or platform action completes while its audit event cannot be written. This applies to every identity including the root.
Deterministic safety mechanisms are unaffected by an audit outage.
No action is queued for later application during an audit outage; on restoration halt-class actions become available with no queue of deferred actions.
An unobservable audit system is treated as unhealthy rather than assumed fine.
A failure in the one-transaction, append-only, or tenant-isolation groups blocks release unconditionally.

A partially validated tenant must never become active. A tenant record that has not completed every mandatory provisioning step remains in a safe draft state in which no user can authenticate, no operational data can be created, no device can enroll, and no work package can be generated.
Onboarding is invitation-driven and there is no public self-signup at V1; pilot tenancies are invitation-only with no public free trial and are functionally identical to a paying tenant.

Rollback is explicit and non-destructive: where provisioning cannot complete the tenant record is returned to the safe draft state with a recorded reason and is never deleted, because nothing on this platform is purged.
The activation control is unavailable until every mandatory provisioning step carries a committed success event in the tenant's audit stream.
Every provisioning step, retry, rollback and activation commits its audit event in the same transaction as the change itself.

Seeding the first Tenant Admin is refused while the isolated data space is unconfirmed, with the outstanding step named; an out-of-order seeding request is rejected as an ordering violation and writes a rejection event.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Console seeding action and platform ordering check

business_rules.statement: All six provisioning steps are idempotent: a repeated request produces no second data space, no second account and no second invitation record.
The tenant-group label is an internal label of the client's team only, with no operational behaviour, and is absent from every response served to any tenant-facing surface.
Authoring under an expired implementation authoring capacity is denied at request time regardless of the grant record's stored state, so the safe outcome does not depend on a background process.
Revoking the implementation authoring capacity leaves all authored content, all versions and all approval history intact — the access ends, the authored content does not.
A measurement screen cannot be submitted for review without lower limit, upper limit, unit and at least one severity mapping.
Training Library content is excluded from every generated work package.
A Workflow declaring a locale cannot publish in that locale while any worker-facing element, including a designated coaching default, is missing in it.
No import path creates a Workflow screen automatically from an uploaded document without passing the full approval chain.

The platform never invents content, rules or thresholds; where no authoritative source exists for a specification limit the screen cannot be submitted, the Workflow is re-scoped, or the work continues on the tenant's existing paper process outside the platform.
An expired, revoked or superseded invitation cannot activate an account.
A failed or abandoned identity proof leaves no partially activated account and no usable credential material.
Requesting an invitation status without an authenticated console session returns no information about whether the account exists.
An invitation is single-use: a second use of the same link after activation is refused.

Sending is not delivery; delivery is not opening; opening is not acknowledgement; acknowledgement is not the business action. The console must never display 'invitation sent' as though it were 'administrator active'.
A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing an authorisation; the invitation does not grant authority by being received.

A looser-than-floor value is rejected inline with the floor stated, and is never accepted, clamped or merely logged. Tenants may make the platform stricter than default; they may never make it looser than the platform floor.
A qualification expiry warning stage cannot be removed or delayed; earlier stages can be added.
The Severity 1 action bundle cannot be reduced below lot freeze, Quality-Manager-only release and escalation; tenants may add actions to any level and may never remove Severity 1's floor.

Scheduling a first Run re-validates the full configuration dependency chain — Site, Area, Shift, Job Type, approver role, published Workflow, qualification requirements — and names any missing element.
Removing the last Tenant Admin is refused, naming the rule.
Removing the last approver-capable role while any Job exists is refused, naming the rule.
A role correction is recorded as a removal event and an addition event, never as an in-place edit.

No surface shows a revocation as in force on a device before that device has acknowledged the command; a revocation is recorded immediately and in force on a device at that device's next sync or at expiry of the offline trust window, whichever comes first.
A worker cannot enter or amend their own qualification on any surface; self-attestation is not permitted.
The Read-only Auditor cannot reach any Client Command Center route.
Segregation of duties: the user who creates a Job cannot approve that same Job, and if the creator also holds the approver role the platform routes approval to a second qualified approver.
Qualification validation runs at assignment, at Run start, and at every screen carrying an override.
A worker may complete the current run at the moment of expiry and cannot be re-assigned to work requiring the expired certification; there is no grace period beyond it.
A recertification whose new expiry does not postdate the previous expiry is refused; back-dating the issue date is allowed with both the certification date and the entry date recorded.
A second clearance in the same Area in the same shift routes to the Quality Manager regardless of worker, because repeated exceptions in one Area are a signal about the Area.
A qualification gate never resolves in the worker's favour because a clearance notification was sent but not delivered; the gate never fails open.
A device below the application-version floor cannot execute a Run; a device below the floor is not a conformant device.
A Run whose package has not staged is shown as not-yet-ready and cannot be entered, rather than silently missing.
Media is evicted from the device only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check, never on the strength of an attempted upload.
Wipe and de-authorisation require root approval and attempt a final sync of pending captures first.

The login is the credential, not the device: a worker's identity, qualifications, language preference and attribution travel with them onto whatever conformant device they pick up, and a shared tablet confers nothing by itself.
No user-interface path creates a Super Admin account; the count of root accounts is exactly one at all times.
A Platform Engineer's mutating change never applies on submission and is visibly pending until an Admin approves it.
No console role, including the root, can disable any of the six ENFORCED platform invariants.
No Studio action creates an atomic capability; adding a capability to the platform is an engineering change in the foundation, not a configuration action.
A Studio outage has no effect on any Run already assigned a pinned work package.
The Author of a submission cannot review it, advance it, or release it; no identity performs two stages on one submission.
The Reviewer cannot edit content; the only corrective path is return-with-comments to the Author, and a return requires a comment.
A screen capable of deviating without an explicit severity mapping cannot be published; the platform never assumes a severity value.
A soft proof gate has no effect on specification-gate behaviour: an out-of-tolerance measurement always registers as a deviation and always classifies a severity.
Mapping a band to Severity 1 renders a non-dismissible consequence notice recorded in the change summary, stating that the automatic lot hold is armed and releasable only by a Quality Manager.
Package generation re-verifies severity mapping coverage for the pinned version rather than trusting the publication-time check.
A version number is created only at publication; a draft has no version number in force and reaches no device, no work package and no Job.
An in-progress Run completes on the version it started on, regardless of any publication during it; version-change notices reach the worker at the boundary of the next execution, never inside a Run.
No surface shows a version as in force on a device before that device has acknowledged the version-change command.
A version cannot be archived while active Jobs reference it; a version is never auto-archived when its Jobs are archived.
Severity is classified at the instant of capture offline, and a Severity 1 classification places the lot hold on the device immediately without waiting for connectivity.
Server-side detection atoms mirror the on-device classification; they are never the trigger.
The absence of coaching assets never blocks a gate or alters a classification.
A worker never sees a sync conflict on any Frontline screen; conflict review is a Client Command Center surface.
The Client Command Center exposes no authoring control and no record edit for any role; four things are deliberately impossible from it for every role.
A skew-flagged conflict routes to Client Command Center review rather than resolving on device timestamp.
No generated element can be submitted while marked unreviewed; clearing the marker is an explicit act per element, not a bulk accept.
The authoring aid cannot write a specification limit, a severity band or a gate setting that the platform will enforce without an author entering or confirming it.
No artificial-intelligence component participates in deviation classification at any point.
A qualification-requirement change applies only to Runs scheduled after publication; active assignments are grandfathered but flagged with a supervisor confirmation and recorded reason.
Every approval-chain transition, publication and adoption commits its audit event in the same transaction as the change.
Validation runs at submission, at publication, and at package generation, with the same rule set, because library pointers may change between them.
A locale failure blocks only that locale; other declared locales publish.
An archived library item referenced by a version blocks package generation rather than producing a package with a dangling reference.
A republish cannot proceed without a description, for every class; the description is stored in the permanent version history and for notified classes does double duty as user-facing text.

A published version's classification and description are immutable; a mis-classification discovered after publication is corrected by a new publication, never by re-labelling, because re-labelling would falsify the audit receipt.
A mis-classified patch is returned by the Reviewer, because the classification decides how the change reaches the floor.

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A surface can perform a business write but cannot reach the audit store
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: For the four online surfaces the action is refused under the one-transaction rule; for the Frontline the local durable append-only queue accepts the audit event alongside the business event
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Frontline queue also cannot accept
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The device blocks the action
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On store or queue restoration; device-originated events reconcile at sync with both timestamps preserved

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The correction event can be written but the recompute fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The correction stands, the recompute is retried, and the record is marked 'Corrected; figures not yet recomputed'
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The recompute cannot complete
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The record shows the correction and the stale figures side by side with the staleness stated; Quality Manager and platform operations raised
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On recompute service restoration; the recompute event names original figures, new figures and the delay

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The local durable append-only queue is unwritable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None is permitted that accepts an unaudited business event
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — there is no second acceptance path by design
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Upload-only mode with capture blocked and existing work preserved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Queue integrity restored, or the device retired and its queue drained through the device recovery path; server compares expected and received pair counts per device session

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The trace store is unavailable while an agent is running
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The decision record is written with the operational record and the trace is marked unavailable for that run
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Neither the trace nor the decision record can be written
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The agent's output is not delivered to any human or record; the surface renders agent unavailability rather than silence
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On store restoration; the gap is stated rather than backfilled with reconstructed reasoning

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The notification audit write fails
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Under the one-transaction rule the notification is not sent
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The audit store is unavailable for the whole notification service
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No notifications are sent; the Command Center feed continues from the event spine; platform operations raised
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On audit store restoration notifications are created from the durable event log with their original event times; the trail shows the delay explicitly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Mirroring into the tenant's log fails while a privileged session is open
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The session continues only if the platform log is writing; the mirror is retried and the session is marked mirroring-delayed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Neither log can be written
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The session is terminated automatically and the termination is raised through the platform incident path
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On log restoration the mirror catches up in event order with original times preserved; the post-session report names the mirroring delay

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The search index is unavailable or stale
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Query the log directly with date and entity filters, accepting slower responses
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The log query itself times out at scale
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A bounded export by date and entity delivered asynchronously, rather than a partial result presented as complete
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On index rebuild; rebuilds are verified against log counts and a discrepancy raises an investigation event

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An export job fails partway
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The job is retried once from the beginning rather than resumed, because a resumed export could silently omit a range
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Repeated failure
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No file is delivered, the failure is stated, and the export audit event records the attempt and its failure
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Narrow the range and retry; no reconciliation required because no partial artifact exists

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tiering run cannot complete
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The records remain hot and the failure is raised
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The tiering service is unavailable for an extended period
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Everything remains hot and retrievable
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On service restoration with the tiering run itself audited; a partial anonymisation run must be resumable, must never re-anonymise, and halts and raises rather than retrying blindly

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The audit store is unavailable
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None exists for halt-class actions by design; for device-originated work the local durable queue is the first fallback and is a genuine audit store
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The device queue also fails, or the outage extends beyond the device trust windows
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Halt-class actions unavailable, device capture blocked with existing work preserved, deterministic safety mechanisms unaffected
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Store restoration then queue drain; expected versus received pair counts per device session reconciled

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Telemetry collection fails, so the audit system is unobserved
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Synthetic checks continue, writing and reading a heartbeat event per log at a fixed interval
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Synthetic checks also fail
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform treats the audit system as unhealthy and enters the graded response of §30D.14
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On telemetry restoration; the observability gap is recorded with its duration

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A release-blocking test cannot pass
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: None; the release does not proceed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not applicable — a blocked release has no further degradation
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The release is held and the defect is worked
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Fix and re-test; the release record names the test, the defect and the fix

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Any provisioning step reports failure or exceeds its operator-visible timeout
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: A bounded, operator-visible retry of the failed step alone, not of the whole sequence
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Rollback itself cannot commit, for instance because the audit service is down — the record is left in ProvisioningFailed, itself a closed state, and raised to the Root Super Admin
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Tenant surfaces closed; no tenant user authenticated; no operational record in existence; the failure recorded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Retry the failed step; on success the sequence resumes at the following step; activation is blocked unless every step carries a committed success event

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Seeding a Tenant Admin or provisioning the implementation authoring role before the isolated data space is confirmed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Prevention: the console refuses the seeding action while the data-space step is not confirmed, naming the outstanding step
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The safe draft rollback of FB-ONB-01
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Tenant closed, no account seeded
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Confirm the data space then re-run the seeding step; the activation gate re-reads the six success events

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An implementation authoring capacity that outlives onboarding
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Automatic expiry of the capacity at the recorded end date
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The expiry job cannot run — the capacity is treated as expired at read time
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The implementation team can read nothing and write nothing in the tenant workspace; the tenant's own users are unaffected and the floor keeps running
failures_fallbacks.recovery: An Admin re-provisions a fresh capacity with a new stated purpose and end date, never a silent revival

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A procedure marked for adaptation has no authoritative source for a specification limit
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The screen is authored without Section 5 populated and cannot be submitted
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Workflow is re-scoped so the unspecified measurement becomes a non-measurement screen
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No Workflow published; no worker executes an unspecified measurement against an invented tolerance
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The tenant supplies the limit; the screen is authored and passes the chain

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The single-channel first invitation fails: provider rejection, bounce, silent non-delivery, expired link, abandoned identity proof, identity-provider misconfiguration
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Resend on the same address
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Reissue to a corrected address, superseding the prior record; then out-of-band contact arranged commercially outside the platform followed by a fresh seeding
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The tenant record sits in awaiting-acceptance indefinitely with no login possible — a stalled onboarding, not an unsafe one
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reissue and activate; the invitation's terminal state is compared with the account's existence

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A tenant activates and tries to run work before its configuration supports it
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Each dependent action refuses with the specific missing configuration named
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where a tenant cannot complete configuration the tenant creates a custom Job Type, available immediately at every tier with no platform approval step
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No Job, no Run, no assignment, no work package, no device execution — the floor does not start half-configured
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Complete the configuration; at the first Run the platform re-validates the full dependency chain

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A wrong role granted and revoked while the user is offline on a Frontline device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The revocation stands centrally and every server-side path refuses the revoked capability immediately, bounding exposure to on-device actions only
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The offline trust window expires and the device forces a sync before further high-risk actions, sign-offs foremost
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The identity holds no server-side authority; the device holds at most the actions its cached window permits before it must sync
failures_fallbacks.recovery: At next sync the device applies the pending command in order; where the person must be stopped now and the device is unreachable, the honest instruction is physical — the Supervisor retrieves the tablet

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Qualification data unavailable at validation: cached state older than the trust window, a clearance not yet delivered, or a clock skewed beyond threshold
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Where the cached state is stale beyond the trust window the device forces a sync before permitting the gated action
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Where no sync is possible the run parks and the worker continues their other assigned runs — a controlled hold, not an override
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No gated step is executed without a valid qualification or a delivered clearance
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Connectivity returns; the clearance or renewal applies in order from the command channel; the parked run resumes

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A work package is not staged at shift start
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Lazy pull when the device is next connected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: On-demand re-pull by the supervisor; then the worker executes a different assigned Run whose package is staged
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No Run executes without its package; the worker is told which Runs are not ready and why
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Connectivity returns; the package stages; the Run becomes ready; per-device package inventory reconciled against assigned Runs

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Loss of the root account: credential loss, multi-factor device loss, identity-provider outage, allowlist misconfiguration, or custody loss
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Recovery of the root's own authentication factors through the client's identity provider — a client-side act, not a platform capability
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Not specified in the Statement of Work; re-creating a root account is by definition a backend act at commissioning
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The platform runs; the critical class is frozen; console user administration stops; nothing unsafe is permitted because the frozen actions are all the dangerous ones
failures_fallbacks.recovery: As decided under DEC-ROOT-001; on recovery the approval queue is reviewed for aged critical requests, none of which applied silently

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The Standards and Operations Studio is unavailable or the author's session is lost
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The draft is preserved and the author resumes; explicit server-side draft autosave with an author-visible last-saved time is proposed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Authoring is deferred; the floor continues on published, pinned versions
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No unpublished content reaches any device; every Run continues on the version it started on
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Service restoration; on resume the draft's last-saved state is compared with the author's local view and divergence is shown rather than merged silently

failures_fallbacks.trigger: No eligible Reviewer or Release Authority for a submission
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The Tenant Admin grants the authoring grant to a second qualified person, which is an audited permission change
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Quality Manager sets a per-workflow Release Authority override; then the submission remains unpublished and the floor continues on the current published version
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No unreviewed content reaches a device; the previously published version remains in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Staffing; aged submissions are visible in the queue with proposed 24/48/72-hour aging highlights

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A screen reaching validation without a severity mapping
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Publication is blocked with the specific screen and the specific missing mapping named
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Reviewer returns the submission with comments; then the Workflow is not published and the prior version stays in force
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No worker ever meets a screen that can deviate without a defined consequence
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The author completes the mapping and resubmits; at package generation the platform re-verifies coverage

failures_fallbacks.trigger: An incomplete screen at submission: missing severity mapping, missing locale variant, an archived library item, or a Section 9 certification that no longer exists
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Submission refused with the screen, the section and the missing element named
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Reviewer returns with comments; then publication is blocked and the prior version stays in force
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor runs on the last complete, approved version
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The author completes and resubmits; at package generation the platform re-resolves every library pointer and locale variant

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A submission stalled in the chain: no eligible Reviewer, unavailable Release Authority, or an author who has left the tenant
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The aging highlights recommended in section 32.2
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Tenant Admin grants the authoring grant to another person or the Quality Manager sets a per-workflow override; then the submission is withdrawn and re-authored by a current employee
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor runs on the last approved version, which is always a safe state because it was approved
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Staffing or withdrawal; the queue must include stalled items rather than hiding them

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A version-change command that does not reach a device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The command remains queued and is applied at the next successful sync, in order
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The supervisor performs an on-demand re-pull; then the device continues on its current pinned version and the Hub shows the Job as not yet adopted
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Work continues on the last approved version in force on that device, stated honestly by both the Command Center and the Hub
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Connectivity returns and the command applies; adoption tracking compares issued commands against per-device acknowledgements

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A coaching asset absent from the package under storage pressure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The authored instruction content already on the screen, which is packaged, serves as the fallback
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The worker proceeds on the instruction text alone; where the worker cannot proceed the hard gate blocks advance and the run stalls at that screen
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No advance without proof; no classification altered; no fabricated coaching
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Connectivity returns and the agent-selected asset becomes available; storage-pressure signals are fleet telemetry

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Two authors on one draft: simultaneous edits with no lease, a lease held by an absent author, or a stale holder writing after the lease lapsed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The lease denies the second writer and shows the holder
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The lease expires on inactivity and the second author takes over, with the fencing token rejecting the first author's late write
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: One coherent draft; no lost work discarded without a human seeing it
failures_fallbacks.recovery: The author re-applies their changes; the draft's revision history shows both attempts

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The authoring aid is unavailable or produces unusable output
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the drafting request once, then proceed without it
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The author writes the content by hand — the no-artificial-intelligence workflow producing an identical, fully compliant result; where a second locale cannot be hand-authored the Workflow publishes in the complete locale only
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Either an approved Workflow authored entirely by people, or no new version and the prior approved version still in force
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Service restoration, or the author's decision to proceed unassisted; no reconciliation required because no record diverged

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A qualification requirement change that strands the shift: no worker on shift holds the new certification, the certification does not exist, or the change is published mid-shift
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The supervisor grants a clearance — Client Command Center action 10 — with a categorised reason; a never-held qualification requires the Quality Manager
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The supervisor reassigns to a qualified worker (action 8); then the Job Owner declines adoption of the notified-class version, keeping the prior version in force
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Work proceeds on the prior approved version, or under an audited clearance, or does not proceed; no unqualified worker executes a gated step silently
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Certification, or adoption; repeated clearances in one Area route to the Quality Manager on the second in a shift

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Validation refusing repeatedly: a library item archived while an author works, a locale declared but never staffed, or a certification renamed
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The author corrects and resubmits
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The author narrows the declared locales, publishing in the complete locale; then the Workflow is withdrawn and the prior version stays in force
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor runs on the last complete approved version
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Correction; the validation set is re-run at package generation so a change after publication cannot reach a device

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A mis-classified version reaching the floor — a notified change published as a patch with no first-screen notice
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Publish a corrective notified-class version whose republish description states the correction
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: The Job Owner declining adoption is NOT permitted because patches auto-adopt; the supervisor reassigns or holds the affected work through Client Command Center actions and the Quality Manager holds the lot
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The floor runs on a version somebody reviewed; the deficiency is a missing notice rather than an unreviewed limit
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Corrective publication; adoption tracking shows exactly which Runs, devices and versions were affected
